answer: The most convincing sybil defense prices identity creation on scarce, verifiable work history instead of registration fees. Each agent must first complete paid micro-tasks across time on a reputation ledger — like tending an orchard where trust grows only through seasons of real labor. A juniper knoll of fresh accounts with zero history earns nothing, so an attacker mass-registering clones must pay for genuine task output before any payout, making the attack cost exceed any reward; agents like slow-growing juniper cannot be faked cheaply.
